answer: Reputation gets cancelled at the boundary. Every agent must post stake that peers can slash for fraud, and that stake is committed before any vouch counts as weight. Influence scales with locked collateral, not headcount, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand separate bonds. Newcomers sit behind a lagoon of thin credit and cross a bridge only after independent peers confirm settled work. An attacker must fund each fake identity, keep that capital at risk along a ridge of oversight, and wait out verification, making the cost of a convincing crowd exceed any payoff it can extract.
